title: Sell Mineral Rights in Uniontown, PA
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Uniontown, PA
metaDescription: Own mineral rights near Uniontown, the Fayette County seat? We buy Marcellus interests directly, explain your division order, and pay cash.
heroLead: Every mineral deed question in Fayette County eventually leads back to the courthouse in Uniontown, which means owners here have an easier time confirming their history than families in the smaller boroughs around them.
intro: Uniontown is the Fayette County seat, home to the recorder of deeds office where nearly every mineral transfer, lease, and probate filing tied to land across the county has to pass through eventually. If your family holds minerals anywhere in Fayette County, chances are the paper trail runs directly through this courthouse, which actually works in your favor when it's time to confirm exactly what you own.

The city itself sits within the Marcellus wet-gas window, and while the busiest well pads in the county tend to sit in the surrounding townships rather than inside city limits, plenty of Uniontown-area families hold interests in tracts just outside town that have seen real drilling activity.

sections.heading: The Advantage of Being Where the Records Are
paragraphs: Because the recorder of deeds and the register of wills both sit in Uniontown, confirming a chain of title or clearing up an old probate matter for a Fayette County interest tends to move faster than in counties where families have to travel or mail requests to a distant courthouse. That's a small but real advantage when you're trying to sell.
It doesn't mean every Uniontown-area deed is simple, though. Coal-era severances, generational splits, and old coke company transfers show up here just as often as anywhere else in the county.

sections.heading: Understanding Your Royalty Statement
paragraphs: If a well near your tract is already producing, your statement should separate gross value, deductions, and net payment. Under Pennsylvania's Guaranteed Minimum Royalty Act, you're entitled to at least one-eighth of gross value, but post-production deductions permitted by your specific lease language, upheld broadly by Kilmer v. Elexco, can still reduce that net check significantly.

sections.heading: How We Make an Offer
paragraphs: We pull your deed history, confirm your interest against current unit and permit filings, review any statements you have, and give you a cash offer grounded in real numbers. There's no pressure to decide on the spot, and we're happy to answer questions before you commit to anything.

faqs.question: Is it easier to confirm my title because I'm near the county seat?
faqs.answer: Often, yes. Records for the whole county are housed at the Fayette County courthouse in Uniontown, which can speed up title confirmation compared to counties with records split across multiple locations.

faqs.question: Are there active wells inside Uniontown city limits?
faqs.answer: Development is more common in the surrounding townships than within the city itself, but we check current permits against your specific parcel regardless of exactly where it sits.

faqs.question: My royalty check seems low compared to the reported gas price. Why?
faqs.answer: Post-production deductions for gathering, compression, and transportation are the most common reason. Reviewing your specific lease language clarifies exactly what's being deducted and why.

faqs.question: Can you help me clear up an old probate issue before we sell?
faqs.answer: Yes. Because the register of wills is also in Uniontown, resolving outstanding probate matters tied to a mineral interest is usually more straightforward here than in other counties.
